title: Implement object-history-03 (history get, restore, destroyed query)
description: No code exists. -03: Foo/get includeReplaced/includeDestroyed with historyAfter/Before/Skip/Limit ignored unless a flag is true; multi-id paging = one call per id; per-version expires in objectHistory; new Foo/set restore argument (final version + optional patch, server-set properties kept; Email/SieveScript/missing-container/conflict notes) replacing create-with-old-id; Foo/changes reports a restored id as updated or created, never destroyed; Foo/query onlyDestroyed/destroyedAfter/destroyedBefore; destruction via other protocols/server counts; non-current versions are not blob references (affects blobHasReference, Blob/lookup, GC).
notes: Decision Mark 2026-11-12: crate-jmap aims to be THE complete reference implementation covering the JMAP specs, so this is required work, not optional. Split rule: the crates own wire types, validation, method semantics and error mapping; storage-, transport- or media-specific work is pushed to the calling crate through backend trait hooks (see the spec-method-defaults memory: no no-op default when that would put wrong data on the wire). Here: method semantics in the crates; history retention and storage are backend hooks.
